result.summary: The FastF1Client class in apps/api/app/services/telemetry/fastf1_client.py is the central data service for F1 telemetry in ApexView. It has 12 public methods that handle session, lap, telemetry, and track data fetching with Parquet caching. The legacy duplicate at apps/api/app/services/fastf1_client.py is dead code—never imported by live code, only the new telemetry subdirectory version is used. The data_service factory returns FastF1Client under LIVE_DATA=true condition. get_telemetry and get_delta_analysis are called exclusively through the Qualifying page flow: frontend calls fetchTelemetry/fetchDelta → /telemetry and /telemetry/delta routes (GET) → data_service.get_data_service() returns FastF1Client → methods invoked. The analysis service (apps/analysis_service) fetches telemetry indirectly via HTTP to /telemetry and /laps/sectors endpoints during scaled-delta, corner-analysis, and performance-insights orchestration. No out-of-scope consumers detected; all are part of the Qualifying analysis flow.

result.summary:
ApexView demonstrates HEAVY use of qualifying telemetry/delta machinery in the Qualifying page. This page exclusively consumes FastF1Client.get_telemetry, FastF1Client.get_delta_analysis, GET /telemetry, GET /telemetry/delta, and analysis-service endpoints (GET /analysis/performance-insights on port 8501) for its core visualizations (TelemetryLine, DeltaPlot, CornerBreakdownPanel, PerformanceInsightsPanel). The Race page uses ONLY pre-computed race-specific endpoints (GET /race/pace, GET /race/tyre-degradation, GET /race/pit-stops, GET /race/team-performance) and does NOT call telemetry or delta machinery. The Practice page uses ONLY pre-computed practice-specific endpoints (GET /practice/long-runs, GET /practice/short-runs, GET /practice/sector-analysis, GET /practice/progression) and does NOT call telemetry or delta machinery. The Home page is static and does NOT consume telemetry. Track Intelligence page is static with editorial content and does NOT call telemetry/delta endpoints. The Transparency page is purely static HTML with no data fetching. Telemetry/delta machinery is architecturally isolated to Qualifying and NOT consumed by other qualifying-adjacent pages (Race, Practice, Home, Track Intelligence, Transparency).

Out-of-scope consumers identified: (None found. All telemetry/delta/performance-insights consumption is contained within the Qualifying page.)

result.summary: The Qualifying page (apps/web/app/qualifying/) obtains telemetry traces from the API /telemetry endpoint, delta/gap data from the unified performance-insights endpoint (which calls analysis service), and performance insights from the analysis service /analysis/performance-insights endpoint. The qualifying page does NOT call the API /telemetry/delta endpoint directly—delta data is embedded exclusively in the performance-insights response. All track data (corners, sectors) comes from the API /track/{round} endpoint. The API base URL is http://localhost:8000 (configurable via NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL env var) and the analysis service is http://localhost:8501 (configurable via NEXT_PUBLIC_ANALYSIS_SERVICE_URL).

result.summary: The ApexView analysis service maintains a frozen API handshake contract with the API service across five primary endpoints (/analysis/scaled-delta, /analysis/corner-analysis, /analysis/technique-profile, /analysis/generate-insight, /analysis/performance-insights). All HTTP communication occurs through two code paths: direct fetches in main.py (lines 343, 359, 546, 562, 882, 898, 1196, 1212) and the performance_orchestrator.py module (lines 379-460). The analysis service exclusively consumes two API endpoints: GET /telemetry (with query params session, drivers, session_part) and GET /laps/sectors (same params). Response fields consumed include: distance, speed, brake, throttle, lapTime, relativeDistance, time (from /telemetry) and totalTime, sector1/2/3 (from /laps/sectors). All request/response models are fully defined in models/schemas.py with precise field names, types, and defaults.

result.summary: ApexView is a F1 engineering telemetry platform with a Next.js frontend, FastAPI backend, and analysis microservice. The telemetry system uses a Parquet-based caching layer for performance. Source code is BAKED INTO THE DOCKER IMAGES (not volume-mounted), meaning container restarts alone won't pick up changes—images must be rebuilt. Cache data is the ONLY volume-mounted directory (/app/data/cache maps to ./data/cache on host). Uvicorn runs without --reload in both services.

result.summary: ApexView monorepo audit complete. MockDataService.get_telemetry returns synthetic telemetry (distance, speed, throttle, brake, gear, rpm, drs arrays) when LIVE_DATA env is False; factory function get_data_service selects between FastF1Client and MockDataService. API tests use direct helper functions (pytest fixtures with mock lap dicts) rather than instantiating FastF1Client/httpx directly, isolating from network. Analysis service tests mock httpx.AsyncClient as AsyncMock with status/json methods; mocks accept arbitrary URLs (tolerant of unknown endpoints), using `.get.return_value` pattern. DeltaResult constructed via keyword arguments in test fixtures (line 92-102). No standalone tools/ directory exists; scripts/ contains validation PowerShell/bash. CI via GitLab (pytest -q invocation); docker-compose defines standard service setup (LIVE_DATA env toggles mock vs live).
